s1.syndrome_frame: Painless scrotal swelling with bilateral testicular enlargement
salient_findings: Large, solid masses in both testes on scrotal ultrasound
Tumor confined to the testis with lymphovascular invasion
key_facts: 63-year-old man
8-month history of painless scrotal swelling
Bilateral testicular enlargement without tenderness
Scrotal ultrasound showed large, solid masses in both testes
Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin, α-fetoprotein, and lactate dehydrogenase were within normal limits
No evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses on PET-CT scan
Left radical inguinal orchiectomy was performed
Tumor size: 7.0 × 6.0 × 4.2 cm
Histologic examination demonstrated a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types

shortlist.label: Mixed germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with multiple cell types and lymphovascular invasion

shortlist.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral testicular enlargement and solid masses on ultrasound

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular tumor with lymphovascular invasion and normal tumor markers

shortlist.label: Embryonal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with multiple cell types and aggressive features

shortlist.label: Spermatocytic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with distinct cell types and testicular origin

raw.rationale: The histologic examination demonstrated a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types, which is consistent with a mixed germ cell tumor, a type of testicular cancer that contains more than one type of germ cell tumor component.

rejected.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
rejected.why: While possible, this diagnosis is too broad and does not specifically account for the presence of multiple distinct cell types.

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Seminomas are typically uniform in cell type and do not usually present with the pleomorphic pattern described.

rejected.label: Embryonal carcinoma
rejected.why: Embryonal carcinomas can be part of a mixed germ cell tumor but alone do not explain the presence of three distinct cell types.

rejected.label: Spermatocytic tumor
rejected.why: Spermatocytic tumors are rare and typically have a distinct histological appearance that does not match the pleomorphic pattern with three distinct cell types described in the case.
